thought.text: Host is Ubuntu 22.04. I'll install `rsync` and write the full build orchestration script (staging + wave-parallel builds):

reasoning_content:
Host is Ubuntu 22.04 with apt-get. Can install node 20 and npm.

Now let me write a complete build orchestration script. Plan:

```
stage <service>: create /tmp/spark-build/<service>/
  1. rsync service directory (exclude .git)
  2. rsync 03-shared-services into service/../../03-shared-services (i.e., /tmp/spark-build/02-backend-<svc>/../)
```

Better directory layout that mimics the monorepo:
/tmp/spark-build/
  02-backend/<svc>/           (copy of the service)
  02-backend/tatbestandsmerkmalsextraction/  (for rechtsquellenvorbereitung)
  03-shared-services/          (copy of all shared, reused across builds)
  demospipes/:
    api/  core/  data-structures/
    addons/bmds/{api,executors,data_structures}/

For services inside demospipes:
- api: copy to /tmp/spark-build/demospipes/api, and place data-structures at /tmp/spark-build/demospipes/data-structures (relative path ../data-structures from api). ✓
- core: same + addons? core's deps: only ../data-structures. ✓
- bmds api: context /tmp/spark-build/demospipes/addons/bmds/api: need ../../../data-structures → /tmp/spark-build/demospipes/data-structures ✓, ../data_structures → /tmp/spark-build/demospipes/addons/bmds/data_structures ✓
- bmds executors: same as api. ✓

Build commands (all from service directory, context = service directory):
- demospipes-base-api: -t demospipes-base-api:latest, Dockerfile at demospipes/api → then also tag as demospipes-base-api:v1.18.127-main-ce4cc11 (for the addon's FROM).
- demospipes-base-executors: tag as :latest + :v1.24.195-main-8a31fa9.
- bmds api: -t demospipes-bmds-api (sed the FROM to local tag).
- bmds executors: -t demospipes-bmds-executors.

Secrets: pass dummy secrets for all builds (harmless where not needed).

Now about the .dockerignore in the staged context: the service's own .dockerignore gets copied along → applies to the staged context. The relative path 03-shared-services doesn't match typical ignore patterns. One risk: patterns like `build/` or `dist/` — the shared services don't have build/ directories. `tests/` isn't ignored. OK.

Also, `tmp_bandit_lock` in dokumentenpruefung — irrelevant.

Frontend sub-images (mfe-fp, mfe-kp, mfe-ewm, mfe-ws, shell): context = 01-frontend/<mfe> (its own directory), but their Dockerfiles COPY package.json/package-lock.json and sibling workspace manifests from the context root (../.. level) → they're broken with their own directory as context too! mfe-ewm/Dockerfile: COPY package.json package-lock.json ./ then COPY shared/package.json, mfe-ewm/package.json. So context has to be 01-frontend (parent). With context 01-frontend and -f mfe-ewm/Dockerfile: .dockerignore = 01-frontend/.dockerignore ✓; COPY . . inside mfe-ewm stage → copies the entire 01-frontend into /app (wasteful but works: /app/mfe-ewm exists, /app/shared exists ✓). npm ci --workspace mfe-ewm --workspace shared --include-workspace-root=false → works with the synced lock ✓.

But wait: with context = 01-frontend, does `COPY . .` in the mfe-ewm Dockerfile copy all of 01-frontend? Yes → /app contains all MFEs + package.json etc. `npm run -w shared build` from /app works. Then `npm run -w mfe-ewm build` ✓.

But: `COPY . .` also copies the service's own Dockerfile etc. — no problem. And .env.production: the main frontend Dockerfile does `COPY shell/.env.deployment shell/.env.production` — mfe-ewm's doesn't; mfe-ewm's build may read .env.production if it exists; the .env files are excluded from the context? Check 01-frontend/.dockerignore: `**/*.log`, node_modules, dist, .git, .cache... .env not excluded! shell/.env.deployment exists in the repo. mfe-ewm's vite build may use .env files if present. If not present in the original, no problem. OK — COPY . . will include whatever is in 01-frontend (excluding .git, node_modules, dist).

Hmm wait, does mfe-ewm/Dockerfile's `npm ci --workspace mfe-ewm --workspace shared --include-workspace-root=false` work with the root package.json that has 10 workspaces? npm with -w flags only installs those workspaces' deps + shared deps. Lock file must contain entries for them ✓ (the regenerated lock covers all).

And with include-workspace-root=false: root deps (root package.json's devDeps, e.g., syncpack?) not installed. husky prepare: root package.json's scripts.prepare=husky → npm ci with --include-workspace-root=false skips root lifecycle scripts? Actually `npm ci` with include-workspace-root=false skips the root project's install (lifecycle scripts) entirely — that's why the Dockerfile uses it (avoids the husky failure!). In the main frontend Dockerfile, `npm ci` (root=true) → prepare → husky not found → but the Dockerfile stumped out /usr/local/bin/husky first (RUN printf ... > /usr/local/bin/husky) — so it worked... in the original. Our failure was only lock sync.

So all frontend sub-images: context 01-frontend, -f <dir>/Dockerfile. Tags: mfe-ewm, mfe-fp, mfe-kp, mfe-ws, shell, frontend (main).

tex2pdf: partial COPY — needs .env? No. Also copies CHANGELOG.md (present at service root ✓), src/cli/pyproject.toml etc. ✓ all within the service directory. Plus bizlog path dep → 03-shared-services must be at context/../../03-shared-services → stage into /tmp/spark-build/02-backend/tex2pdf-service with 03-shared-services at /tmp/spark-build/. Wait, tex2pdf root pyproject path: ../../03-shared-services/bizlog (from /tmp/spark-build/02-backend/tex2pdf-service → /tmp/spark-build/03-shared-services ✓). And src/api: ../../../../03-shared-services/bizlog → /tmp/spark-build/../../03-shared-services?? No: from src/api → 4 levels up = /tmp/spark-build → /tmp/spark-build/03-shared-services? Let me compute: src/api/../../.. = tex2pdf-service, /../../../../ = /tmp/spark-build/02-backend? Hmm: src/api → up1: src → up2: tex2pdf-service → up3: 02-backend → up4: /tmp/spark-build. So ../../../../03-shared-services/bizlog = /tmp/spark-build/03-shared-services/bizlog ✓ same location.

But note: uv only resolves the workspace root (tex2pdf-service/pyproject.toml) — members' path deps matter during workspace resolution ✓ both point to the same location.

Now, the staging script:

```bash
SB=/tmp/spark-build
mkdir -p $SB/02-backend $SB/03-shared-services $SB/demospipes
rsync -a --exclude '.git' /workspace/03-shared-services/ $SB/03-shared-services/
for svc in <27 backend services except demospipes>; do
  rsync -a --exclude '.git' --exclude '.venv' --exclude 'node_modules' /workspace/02-backend/$svc/ $SB/02-backend/$svc/
done
rsync -a --exclude '.git' /workspace/02-backend/tatbestandsmerkmalsextraction/ $SB/02-backend/tatbestandsmerkmalsextraction/  # already in the list? has no Dockerfile; needed only for rechtsquellenvorbereitung
# demospipes:
for d in api core data-structures; do rsync -a /workspace/02-backend/demospipes/$d/ $SB/demospipes/$d/; done
for d in api executors data_structures; do rsync -a /workspace/02-backend/demospipes/addons/bmds/$d/ $SB/demospipes/addons/bmds/$d/; done
```

Wait — 03-shared-services is placed at $SB/03-shared-services, and services at $SB/02-backend/<svc> → relative path ../../03-shared-services from $SB/02-backend/<svc> = $SB/03-shared-services ✓.

But wait — is rsync installed? Ubuntu 22.04 usually has rsync. Verify; if not, cp -a.

Also: does the service directory's .dockerignore affect the staged shared service? The service directory's .dockerignore is at the context root ✓ (context = $SB/02-backend/<svc>, its .dockerignore gets copied along). Patterns like `build/` — no build directory in shared. `dist/` — none. OK.

One more: dokumentenaufbereitung-data-service's Dockerfile: `COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./` then `COPY . .` — wait, the earlier grep: line 12: COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./, line 13: COPY . . — no bind mount. But uv sync --no-cache --dev --no-install-project without --locked?? From the earlier output: `uv sync --no-cache --dev --no-install-project` — hmm, without --locked, uv sync uses the lock if present, or updates. No problem.

Now, let me also recheck `fristenmanagement`'s Dockerfile — its line 32: FROM uv AS test-deps, then `uv sync --locked --no-install-project --dev` after `COPY . /app` (line 40-46)? Order: builder at lines 17-28 with bind mount (uv.lock+pyproject bind, secrets, cache), line 25 COPY . /app... anyway — all standard; works from staged directory.

Build queue with resource limits. 8 CPUs, 7.6GB RAM. Builds are mostly network + CPU light (uv compile). torch download in dokumentenaufbereitung-monorepo is about 2-8GB? torch CPU wheel ~200MB + nvidia ~2.5GB + easyocr models ~100MB + docling models ~500MB + HF tokenizer. Heavy but doable.

Concurrency: run up to 3 concurrent builds; 6 waves total:
W1 (now): demospipes-base-api, demospipes-base-executors, dokumentenpruefung (validation build with 6 shared deps)
W2: demospipes-bmds-api, demospipes-bmds-executors (after W1), frontend
W3: frontend sub-images ×5 (mfe-fp, mfe-kp, mfe-ewm, mfe-ws, shell) — after frontend? Independent; but all npm ci... each ~2-5min. Run 3 at a time.
W4: ki-guv-explainability, ki-guv-ai-testing, ki-guv-feedback
W5: berichtskonfigurator, decision-log-store-service, demos-einwendungsmanagement
W6: dokumentensuche, kommentar-service, nachforderungen
W7: ner-extraction, norm-matching, fristenmanagement
W8: graph-api, request-proxy, risikohinweis-service
W9: subsumtion-service, xoev-adapter, dokumentenschwaerzung-orchestrator, dokumentenschwaerzung-pdf-pii-detector
W10: dokumentenaufbereitung-data-service, rechtsquellenvorbereitung
W11: dokumentenaufbereitung-monorepo (heavy, alone)
W12: tex2pdf-service (heavy, alone)

37 total images.

Write the orchestrator: a bash script with a queue; each build: stage (fast) → docker build with log + result line. Run in the background, poll.
